extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy (Schopenhauer), scholars of moral/metaphysical psychology
extracted.subtask_description: Close analytic exposition of sexual love as a manifestation of the will-to-live and of instinct serving the species; identifies the aims, mechanisms, and concrete criteria that guide sexual selection and passion. This is a chapter-length philosophical treatment rather than an empirical scientific guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultimate end of sexual love
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate end of all love affairs is the composition of the next generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the key of the problem: love’s seriousness and sublime elements arise because love determines the existence and special nature of future persons. The chapter repeatedly treats sexual love as essentially directed toward producing a definite individual (the child) whose nature is fixed by the selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of individualisation increases passion
rubrics_metrics.description: The more individualised the choice (i.e., the more exclusively suited the loved individual is to satisfy the chooser’s need for a particular offspring), the stronger the passion will be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A really passionate love is rare because it requires a particularly perfect mutual adaptation of two individualities; the degree of individualisation explains the range from ordinary amorousness to the highest vehemence (described as extremes such as 'Αφροδιτη πανδημος' and 'ουρανια').

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual instinct functions as 'sense of the species' (an illusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instinct implants an illusion so that actions which serve the species appear to the individual as serving his or her own ends; the sexual selection instinct is such an illusion directed to perpetuating the type of the species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature makes individuals believe they pursue individual pleasure while in truth they are guided to secure the best possible progeny. Examples and analogies: birds building nests, insects depositing eggs, and human lovers experiencing a delusive ecstasy that serves species preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary immediate end is possession/physical enjoyment (not reciprocation)
rubrics_metrics.description: In actual cases the essential matter is not reciprocation of love but possession — the physical enjoyment; reciprocation does not console for lack of physical possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence cited includes forced marriages, purchase of favors, and rape; the manner of attaining the end (possession) is secondary to the true end (begetting a particular child). The text emphasises the primacy of possession in many love situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age preference (reproductive window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual attraction generally accords with reproductive capacity: from menarche to menopause, with decided preference for the period from the eighteenth to the twenty-eighth year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit numeric preference is given: outside these years women cease to attract (older women who no longer menstruate excite aversion). The unconscious end is reproduction; attraction declines in proportion to being removed from the fittest period for begetting or conceiving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health (heritable disease)
rubrics_metrics.description: Health is a guiding consideration: acute diseases only temporarily disturb attraction, but chronic diseases or cachexia repel because they are transmissible to the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection disfavors transmissible or chronic conditions; the sexual instinct privileges qualities promising healthy offspring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton/figure/proportion as basis of species type
rubrics_metrics.description: The skeleton is the basis of the type of the species; a straight, well-proportioned figure is strongly preferred, while deformity, disproportion, stunted or dumpy figures, and an abnormal gait repel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text asserts that even a very beautiful face cannot atone for a deformed figure; conversely a strikingly beautiful figure can make up for other defects. Small feet are emphasised as an essential character of the species (quote from Jesus Sirach used as illustration). The importance of proportion, bone-structure, and gait is repeatedly stressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small feet and specific bodily markers (heritability signals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain specific bodily markers — notably small feet — are valued because they signal species-typical traits and are hereditary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small feet are singled out as an essential characteristic of human species-typical locomotion (plantigrade with small tarsus/metatarsus) and are culturally prized as an index of the proper type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teeth as important hereditary feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Teeth are important because they are essential for nourishment and are especially hereditary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Healthy, well-formed teeth are part of the criteria that guide sexual selection owing to their role in offspring viability and heredity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fullness of flesh (plumpness) as signal of nutritive capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain fullness of flesh (predominance of the vegetative function, plasticity) is preferred because it promises abundant nourishment for the foetus; great leanness repels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical plumpness indicates capacity for nourishing offspring; extreme thinness is unattractive for this reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementarity and correction of one-sided qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative considerations guide choice: partners may be selected to correct or neutralise one-sided qualities and abnormities in each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes preference for traits that complement the chooser’s deficiencies (e.g., little men love big women, fair persons like dark). The sexual sense often values perfections that the chooser lacks, and mate-pairing can neutralise asymmetries to produce a more harmonious offspring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual attraction as signal of harmonious progeny (and aversion as signal of inharmonious progeny)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutual attraction indicates that the two individuals are well-suited to produce a harmonious, well-composed child; persistent aversion signals that any child produced would be inharmonious or ill-organised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text claims that mutual liking reflects the will-to-live’s selection for a particular individual—and conversely that dislike or enmity between two people is evidence that the offspring they would produce would be badly organized; examples and literary references (Calderon’s Semiramis) are used to support this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex differences in mating behavior (male inconstancy vs female constancy)
rubrics_metrics.description: By nature the man is inclined to inconstancy (seeking variety) and the woman to constancy, owing to their different reproductive capacities; faithfulness is artificial for men and natural for women, and female adultery is thus less pardonable objectively and subjectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning based on biological fecundity: a man can beget many children in a year while a woman can conceive only one per year; hence natural selection favors male promiscuity and female retention of a protector/nourisher for future offspring.
